# My plan for this year

I'm sitting here with the field notebook I've kept since the early '90s. At 62, I've seen a lot — the shift from flood irrigation everywhere to metered wells, the old local wheat varieties giving way to Jimai and Shannong lines, the cotton boom and bust. My wife and I work the 16.1 mu ourselves, and our son is in Handan in a factory job. So labor is tight — that's the first thing I think about before anything else.

## Field allocation

I split the land roughly like this, same as the last three years because it's been working:

- **10 mu in wheat-maize double cropping** — the flatter plots near the canal road, good soil, easy to get the combine in. This is the backbone.
- **6.1 mu in cotton (single crop)** — the sandier western block. Wheat doesn't do as well there and cotton tolerates it. I know everyone in the village has been pulling out of cotton because of labor, but I've kept a bit because the price picked up last year and I have a buyer I trust in Linqing.

## Winter wheat (10 mu) — already planted last October

Sowed Jimai 22 in the first week of October at about 12.5 kg/mu. Good stand came up before the freeze. I applied 40 kg/mu of compound (15-15-15) as base, plus 15 kg diammonium phosphate — works out to about 8 kg N, 10 kg P₂O₅, 6 kg K₂O in the base. Standard for me.

Now in spring: I'll topdress about **12 kg N/mu as urea at jointing** (late March), maybe a small second shot of 4-5 kg N at heading if the canopy looks thin. That brings my season total to roughly **24 kg N/mu**. I know the extension station pushes 18 kg, but on my soil and with the yields I target (500 kg/mu), I've always needed a bit more. Last year I got 510 kg/mu — I'll push for the same.

Irrigation: greening water in March, jointing water end of April, grain-filling water in mid-May. Three rounds, about 40 m³/mu each. The meter doesn't lie and the electricity keeps going up, so I don't waste. Skip the overwinter irrigation — plenty of soil moisture from November rains this season.

Pesticide: one spray for aphids at heading, one for powdery mildew if humidity spikes. Herbicide was done in late winter.

## Summer maize (10 mu) — after wheat in mid-June

Direct-seed Zhengdan 958 the day after wheat harvest — no-till with the seed drill I share with my nephew. About 4,500 plants/mu. Turnaround is tight, maybe 3-4 days, and at my age I'm not breaking my back tilling.

Fertilizer: 30 kg/mu compound (15-15-15) at planting with the seed drill, then **15 kg N as urea at V6-V8** (around late July). That's about 15 kg N/mu total. Maize is efficient if timed right. I've tried splitting the topdress into two shots in wetter years — probably won't this year unless rain pushes me.

Irrigation: one shot at tasseling (early August) if the August rains don't come. Most years I get away with zero or one. The deep roots on 958 help.

Pesticide: herbicide at planting (atrazine + acetochlor mix). Fall armyworm spray if I see damage — the extension people warned us last summer and the pressure is real now. Budget 40 yuan/mu for that.

Target yield: **520 kg/mu**. Got 540 last year in a good rain year, 480 the year before in drought.

## Cotton (6.1 mu) — plant late April

This is where my decisions look different from a younger farmer. Cotton eats labor — thinning, pruning, multiple picks. With just me and my wife, I've simplified: I plant transgenic Bt cotton (Jimian 958) and I skip the topping and pruning that my father's generation did. Yield is a bit lower but the time savings matter.

- Seed: about 1.5 kg/mu of delinted seed, 70 yuan/mu
- Plastic mulch + drip tape: 90 yuan/mu — I've gone to drip on cotton the last five years, cuts my irrigation water by half and the weeds by a lot
- Fertilizer: **14 kg N/mu, 8 kg P₂O₅, 10 kg K₂O** — cotton likes potassium, and over-nitrogen gives you stalks without bolls. Base 30 kg compound at planting, topdress 20 kg urea at squaring, another 10 kg at flowering
- Irrigation: 2 times via drip, at squaring and peak flowering
- Pesticide: Bt handles bollworm, but I still need to spray for aphids and whitefly twice, and spider mites if it's dry

Picking: I'll pay hired labor for the first and second picks — about 15 person-days at 150 yuan/day. Third pick my wife and I do ourselves. Target **260 kg lint/mu**.

## Budget check

With fertilizer prices where they are and electricity for pumping what it is, I need about 18,000 yuan in cash for inputs this year. I have it from last year's maize and cotton sales. No credit needed, which is how I like it.
